nodes.label: Parallelize table-level validation with a bounded ThreadPoolExecutor
nodes.rationale: Project/main.py validated tables strictly sequentially even though tables are independent (separate connections/output files). Decision: run tables concurrently via a bounded concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor (MAX_TABLE_WORKERS, default 4) because per-table work is I/O-bound (network round-trips), not CPU-bound, so the GIL releases during waits. Rejected multiprocessing (no benefit since bottleneck is I/O not CPU, would need file-locking instead of threading.Lock) and asyncio (bigger surface change across every Project/db/*.py connector for the same win threads already give). Required extracting _validate_table() to avoid non-atomic += across threads, and adding threading.Lock() around shared summary/audit file writes.
